tests.name: Disable Microsoft Defender Firewall
tests.description:
Disables the Microsoft Defender Firewall for the current profile.
Caution if you access remotely the host where the test runs! Especially with the cleanup command which will re-enable firewall for the current profile...

tests.name: Disable Microsoft Defender Firewall via Registry
tests.description:
Disables the Microsoft Defender Firewall for the public profile via registry
Caution if you access remotely the host where the test runs! Especially with the cleanup command which will re-enable firewall for the current profile...

tests.name: Allow SMB and RDP on Microsoft Defender Firewall
tests.description:
Allow all SMB and RDP rules on the Microsoft Defender Firewall for all profiles.
Caution if you access remotely the host where the test runs! Especially with the cleanup command which will reset the firewall and risk disabling those services...

tests.name: Opening ports for proxy - HARDRAIN
tests.description:
This test creates a listening interface on a victim device. This tactic was used by HARDRAIN for proxying.

reference: https://www.us-cert.gov/sites/default/files/publications/MAR-10135536-F.pdf

tests.name: Open a local port through Windows Firewall to any profile
tests.description: This test will attempt to open a local port defined by input arguments to any profile

tests.name: Allow Executable Through Firewall Located in Non-Standard Location
tests.description: This test will attempt to allow an executable through the system firewall located in the Users directory

tests.name: Stop/Start UFW firewall
tests.description: Stop the Uncomplicated Firewall (UFW) if installed.

tests.name: Stop/Start Packet Filter
tests.description: Stop the Packet Filter if installed.

tests.name: Stop/Start UFW firewall systemctl
tests.description: Stop the Uncomplicated Firewall (UFW) if installed, using systemctl.

tests.name: Turn off UFW logging
tests.description: Turn off the Uncomplicated Firewall (UFW) logging.

tests.name: Add and delete UFW firewall rules
tests.description: Add and delete a rule on the Uncomplicated Firewall (UFW) if installed and enabled.

tests.name: Add and delete Packet Filter rules
tests.description: Add and delete a rule on the Packet Filter (PF) if installed and enabled.

tests.name: Edit UFW firewall user.rules file
tests.description: Edit the Uncomplicated Firewall (UFW) rules file /etc/ufw/user.rules.

tests.name: Edit UFW firewall ufw.conf file
tests.description:
Edit the Uncomplicated Firewall (UFW) configuration file /etc/ufw/ufw.conf 
which controls if the firewall starts on boot and its logging level.

tests.name: Edit UFW firewall sysctl.conf file
tests.description:
Edit the Uncomplicated Firewall (UFW) configuration file for setting network 
variables /etc/ufw/sysctl.conf.

tests.name: Edit UFW firewall main configuration file
tests.description:
Edit the Uncomplicated Firewall (UFW) main configuration file for setting 
default policies /etc/default/ufw.

tests.name: Tail the UFW firewall log file
tests.description:
Print  the last 10 lines of the Uncomplicated Firewall (UFW) log file 
/var/log/ufw.log.

tests.name: Disable iptables
tests.description:
Some Linux systems may not activate ufw, but use iptables for firewall rules instead. (ufw works on top of iptables.) 
Attackers cannot directly disable iptables, as it is not implemented as a service like ufw. But they can flush all iptables 
rules, which in fact "disable" iptables.

tests.name: Modify/delete iptables firewall rules
tests.description:
Instead of completely "disabling" iptables, adversaries may choose to delete a certain rule, which, for example, blocks data exfiltration via ftp.
By doing so, they may cause less noise to avoid detection.

tests.name: LockBit Black - Unusual Windows firewall registry modification -cmd
tests.description: An adversary tries to modify the windows firewall registry

tests.name: LockBit Black - Unusual Windows firewall registry modification -Powershell
tests.description: An adversary tries to modify the windows firewall registry.

tests.name: Blackbit - Disable Windows Firewall using netsh firewall
tests.description: An adversary tries to modify the windows firewall configuration using the deprecated netsh firewall command (command still works).

tests.name: ESXi - Disable Firewall via Esxcli
tests.description: Adversaries may disable the ESXI firewall via ESXCLI

tests.name: Set a firewall rule using New-NetFirewallRule
tests.description: This test will attempt to create a new inbound/outbound firewall rule using the New-NetFirewallRule commandlet.

tests.name: ESXi - Set Firewall to PASS Traffic
tests.description: This test sets the default ESXi firewall action to PASS instead of DROP. This allows all incoming and outgoing traffic.
